Summary: AeroMesh builds low-latency inference stacks for drone teleoperation and edge robotics. Very latency- and cost-sensitive; primary goal is deterministic control loop (<50ms p99 ideally) while keeping cloud/TCO manageable. Interested in Redwood's Dedicated/Private options + Optimize for batching/caching/quantization guidance.

Recent timeline:
- 2025-01-15: Intro call (Maya + Diego). High level use-case: remote piloting assistance + automatic shorthand command generation. They described jittery cellular links; local inference preferred.
- 2025-01-22: Technical deep dive with infra (Diego, infra lead Tom). Discussed sequence lengths (mostly 16-64 tokens), sparse long requests for mission summaries (256-512).
- 2025-01-28: Sent perf harness (attached) and sample telemetry traces. They supplied a 2-week trace of real commands.
- 2025-02-11: Demo + requirements workshop (Fireflies ff_20250211_ae-demo-54jK). Key ask: show p50/p95/p99 tradeoffs when enabling batching vs single-shot.
- 2025-02-18: Security questionnaire submitted; legal flagged export-control + residency for flight telemetry.

POC requirements / technical details:
- Workload mix: 85% short command inference (<=64 tokens), 10% sensor-summary (<=256 tokens), 5% longer mission summaries (<=512 tokens).
- Target SLOs: tail latency p99 <= 50ms for command path; p95 <= 25ms desirable. Throughput target ~300 req/s sustained per cluster for 3 simultaneous clusters during peak.
- Cost sensitivity: want cost per 1M tokens to be within 40-60% of current in-house GPU TCO. Open to aggressive quantization if quality delta < 1.5% on their eval set.
- Model preferences: compact causal models (distilled Llama-family variants), and a custom fine-tuned 7B variant. Want fallback to a larger 13B during drop-in periods but with higher cost.
- Optimize interest: batching (dynamic batching with tight latency budget), prefix/KV caching for repeated context (telemetry+state), int8/4-bit quantization experiments, and per-route routing policies to prefer on-prem instances for control path.
- Perf benchmarking ask: Redwood to run benchmark across three configs: (1) Dedicated on small cluster with int8 quant, (2) Dedicated with continuous batching + kv-cache, (3) Private on-prem with conservative quant (int8->4-bit sweep). Evaluate p50/p95/p99, throughput, and cost per 1k tokens. Provide artifacts: flamegraphs, per-token latency breakdown, and configuration recipes.

Quote snippets from stakeholders:
- "We need control path jitter to be non-thing — if inference hiccups, operator trust goes away." — Head of Product
- "If you can show a reliable 50ms p99 and a predictable cost model, this is procurement-ready." — CTO

Next steps (short):
- Redwood to schedule perf bench kickoff (SE + infra). Need confirmation on test harness access and credentials.
- Legal: provide vendor security FAQ + export-control checklist. Drive doc link above.
- Internal: run network latency sampling at 6 edge sites and upload traces by 2025-02-25.

Open questions / blockers:
- How deterministic can Dedicated be under noisy neighbor workloads? (echo: need isolation guarantees).
- Quantization accuracy: they want an evaluation metric and acceptance threshold.
- Export control: need checklist from Redwood before procurement signs off.

Stubs/links: pricing deck - drive://redwood/decks/dedicated-pricing-v2.pdf; perf harness - drive://aeromesh/POC/perf-harness-v1.zip; security FAQ - drive://aeromesh/security/audit-faq-2025.pdf

AE notes / playbook hints:
- Emphasize on-prem deployment + private control plane. Offer to run the three perf configs and deliver a short executive summary + deep-dive appendix. Push Redwood Optimize for caching suggestions (they're eager for KV/prefix caching wins). Keep procurement timeline target 2025-06.
